title: Pedigree analysis
examples: How do I know if a trait is dominant or recessive from a pedigree?
What does it mean when I see a trait skipping generations on a chart?
Can you show me an example of a sex-linked trait on a pedigree?

explain.say: A pedigree chart shows how traits pass through families.
We use symbols to represent males and females in the chart.
A filled-in shape usually indicates the presence of the trait.

items: Filled shape means the trait shows up.
Unfilled shape means the trait does not show up.

explain.say: If a trait appears in every generation, it suggests a dominant pattern.
If a trait skips generations, it might be controlled by a recessive gene.
In real life, tracking traits helps predict risks in families.

faq.q: What does it mean if the trait only shows up in males?
faq.a: It might suggest a sex-linked trait affecting the X chromosome. You could also ask about X-linked inheritance or sex-linked patterns.
asks: Is this trait only passed through fathers?
Does the sex of the person matter for this trait?

faq.q: How do I tell if a trait is dominant or recessive just by looking at the chart?
faq.a: Look for traits that skip generations; this often points toward recessive inheritance. You might also ask about skipping generations or recessive markers.
asks: What pattern suggests a recessive gene?
Can I use the chart to guess the gene type?

faq.q: If two parents do not have the trait, but their child does, what is the pattern?
faq.a: This strongly suggests that both parents are carriers of a recessive gene. You could also ask about carrier parents or recessive expression.
asks: What do parents with no trait passing it on to a child?
Are the parents carriers in this situation?

faq.q: Does the pattern change if the trait is linked to sex?
faq.a: Yes, sex-linked traits follow patterns based on the X or Y chromosomes. You should check if the trait affects males and females differently.
asks: How does sex affect the inheritance pattern?
Are there patterns specific to males or females?

faq.q: Can I use this chart to find the exact gene location?
faq.a: No, pedigree analysis only shows patterns of inheritance, not the exact physical location of the gene. You might ask about gene mapping or physical location.
asks: Does this tell me the chromosome number?
Is the gene on a specific chromosome shown?

facts: Pedigree charts track traits across multiple generations.
A trait that appears in every generation is often dominant.
A trait skipping generations suggests recessive inheritance.
Symbols are used to denote sex: circles for females, squares for males.

quiz.say: If a trait appears in every single generation shown, what is the most likely pattern?
quiz.why: Dominant traits usually appear in every generation because at least one dominant allele is present.

wrong.0: Sex-linked traits are determined by the sex chromosomes, not just the general pattern.
wrong.1: Polygenic traits involve many genes, which is a different level of complexity.
wrong.3: Recessive traits often skip generations because two copies of the recessive allele must be present.

quiz.say: A trait that appears in a child whose parents do not have it suggests what about the parents?

options.show: One parent is dominant, one is recessive
options.say: One parent is dominant, one is recessive

options.show: They do not carry the gene
options.say: They do not carry the gene

quiz.why: If the trait is recessive, both parents must carry the hidden recessive allele to pass it on.

wrong.0: If they were both homozygous recessive, the child would also have the trait.
wrong.1: This combination usually results in the dominant trait showing up.
wrong.2: If they did not carry the gene, the child could not inherit it.

quiz.say: If the trait only affects males in the family tree, what is the pattern likely related to?
quiz.why: Traits restricted to one sex often involve the sex chromosomes, like the X chromosome.

wrong.0: Polygenic traits involve multiple genes across the whole body.
wrong.1: Mitochondrial traits are passed only through the mother, not just restricted to males.
wrong.3: Autosomal traits affect males and females equally regardless of sex.
